evals.name: vague-request-gets-a-brief
evals.prompt: listing invoices is really slow for big organisations, can you make it faster
evals.expected_output: Opens with a brief: goal (listing invoices stays fast for large organisations), scope (the list path in src/billing and src/db; not other endpoints), a measurable acceptance line (a timing or complexity target checked by a named test or measurement), assumptions marked as such, and risks. Asks at most two questions or states assumptions, and reads the list path (listInvoices filters every invoice in memory) before changing code.
expectations: Starts with a brief that has a goal, a scope with something explicitly out of scope, and an acceptance line
The acceptance line is measurable (a number, a test or a command), not 'faster'
Asks at most two questions, or states its assumptions instead of asking
Reads the list path (src/db.mjs or src/billing/invoices.mjs) before proposing a fix, rather than guessing an optimisation

evals.name: risky-change-planned-and-reviewed
evals.prompt: Let organisation admins void an invoice, and keep a record of who voided it and when.
evals.expected_output: Writes a brief that names the risk (authorisation: only admins of the invoice's own organisation; an audit record that cannot be forged), plans before editing (the route, the role and organisation check, the record), writes negative tests (a non-admin, and an admin of another organisation, are refused), implements, runs the tests, and has the change reviewed by a security reviewer before calling it done; reports against the acceptance line.
expectations: The brief names authorisation (role or organisation scoping) as a risk
Plans the change before editing, including the role check and the organisation check
Writes or names tests that a non-admin and an admin of another organisation are refused
Requests a security review (the security-reviewer agent or the security skill's review mode) before reporting done
Reports against the acceptance line, including anything it could not verify

evals.name: small-fix-stays-small
evals.prompt: Fix the typo 'Invoce' in the 404 message in src/server.mjs.
evals.expected_output: Fixes the typo directly with at most a one-line brief, runs the relevant check (the test suite), and reports in a line or two. No plan document, no subagents, no questions.
expectations: Fixes the typo in src/server.mjs without writing a multi-section plan or spawning review agents
Asks no questions
Runs or names a relevant check after the edit
Reports in a few lines

evals.name: feature-with-tests
evals.prompt: Add an endpoint that exports an organisation's invoices as CSV, with tests.
evals.expected_output: Brief with scope (a new GET route and a CSV formatter; not PDF or scheduled exports) and acceptance (a test for the CSV body, the headers including Content-Disposition, and that another organisation's invoices never appear). Plans the steps, names CSV injection or large exports as a risk, builds in steps with the tests run between them, gets a review, and reports with the evidence.
expectations: The brief's scope names the new route and excludes something explicit
Scopes the export to the caller's organisation and tests that another organisation's invoices are absent
Names CSV injection, escaping, or large exports as a risk
Runs the tests after the last edit and reports the result
Requests a code review or security review before reporting done

evals.name: pr-per-task-cycle
evals.prompt: The date filter on the reports page ignores the end date. Fix it. (.agents/sdlc.config.json sets workflow.pullRequests to "per-task"; integration branch develop; you are on develop with a clean tree.)
evals.expected_output: Briefs the fix in a line or two, then opens the cycle before the first edit: a feature branch from develop and a draft pull request carrying the brief. Fixes the filter with a test for the end date, runs the checks after the last edit, then lands the pull request (ready, checks green, squash merge, branch deleted, back on develop) and reports with the PR URL.
expectations: Opens a draft pull request on a new branch before the first edit
Adds or updates a test that covers the end date
Runs the checks after the last edit
Merges the pull request and deletes the branch, ending on develop
The report includes the PR URL

evals.name: agreed-plan-goes-to-the-implementer
evals.prompt: The plan is agreed, build it: 1. in src/billing/invoices.mjs add markPaid(orgId, id) that sets status 'paid' on an open invoice of that organisation and throws on any other status; 2. add POST /invoices/:id/pay to src/server.mjs behind requireAuth, 404 when the invoice is not the caller's; 3. tests in test/invoices.test.mjs for paying an open invoice, paying twice, and another organisation's invoice; 4. run npm test.
evals.expected_output: Does not re-plan or re-ask what the plan decided. Hands the building to the implementer agent, a step per call (or the steps in order), instead of typing the code in the main conversation; checks each report (the step's check, the files changed). Runs npm test after the last edit, and reports against the plan with who built which step and on which tier.
expectations: Hands the build steps to the implementer agent rather than writing the code itself in the main conversation
Does not re-plan or ask questions the agreed plan already answers
Runs the tests after the last edit and reports the result
The report says who built which step (for example: build: implementer ×3, medium)
